subject: English
passage: Traditional marketing theory holds that presenting product recommendations from industry professionals increases those recommendations' persuasive power. When consumer behavior researcher Rui Gao and her colleagues tested advertisements for financial planning services, however, they found that participants in their study judged endorsements from previous clients as significantly more persuasive than endorsements from certified financial advisors (i.e., industry professionals). One reason for this may be that the advisors' status as industry professionals wasn't dismissed but rather was outweighed by participants' views of the practical relevance of the two types of endorsers; that is, participants may have reacted the way they did because ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: endorsements from previous clients portrayed financial planning services as being more affordable than did endorsements from certified advisors.
choices.B: participants did not have enough expertise to evaluate the credibility of the advisors' endorsements but did have enough expertise to evaluate the credibility of previous clients' endorsements.
choices.C: the fact that previous clients had navigated the same financial decisions that participants were contemplating while advisors had not was more important to participants than the advisors' status as industry professionals was.
choices.D: participants regarded the perspectives of both the advisors and previous clients as relevant to financial planning decisions but were skeptical of the advisors' status as industry professionals.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it presents the conclusion that most logically follows from the text's discussion of how participants considered endorsements from previous clients and certified advisors. The text first establishes that recommendations from industry professionals typically increase the persuasive power of those recommendations. However, the text goes on to describe a situation that goes against this expectation: the endorsements from previous clients were judged as more persuasive than the endorsements from certified financial advisors when advertising financial planning services. The text then goes on to speculate as to why this may have been the case, stating that participants likely considered the endorsements from the previous clients to be more convincing than the endorsements from the advisors because the previous clients were perceived as having undergone the same financial decisions that the participants were considering. It is reasonable to infer, then, that participants regarded the previous clients' direct experience as more important to their decision-making than the advisors' status as industry professionals.
